YES

The slicing is correct: for the fused `query_key_value` tensors `keep_index(1, 6144, 768)` yields rows `0..3839` then `4608..6143` in ascending order, and for `attention.dense.weight` `index_select` on dim 1 with `keep_index(1, 2048, 256)` keeps columns `0..1279`, `1536..2047`. All 16 layers are covered, no other tensors are touched, names are preserved, the four required checks are asserted before writing, and the output is a single `out/T2/model.safetensors`. The one thing I cannot verify from reading alone is the unshown `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` helper, which must preserve the float16 dtype and all 244 keys for the bit-exact grade to pass.
